newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: Police in Timor detain seven after soldier's death.
newsitem.headline: Police in Timor detain seven after soldier's death.

text.p: Police in East Timor said on Friday they had detained seven people in connection with the murder of a soldier who was beaten to death by a crowd outside the cathedral in the capital Dili on Christmas eve.

East Timor police chief Colonel Yusuf Muharam told reporters that seven people had been detained as part of the investigation into the death of Corporal Alfredo Siga on December 24. He gave no further details.
Siga was set upon by youths outside the cathedral as a crowd of tens of thousands gathered to welcome Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo after he travelled to Europe to receive the award.
He was one of nine soldiers and police, including Dili's police chief, attacked on that day.

The military says Siga, who was wearing civilian clothes, was attacked while on Christmas leave. But residents said he was targeted when he was found carrying a pistol after rumours that an attempt would be made on Belo's life.
Two other people were detained by police on Tuesday when they were found by Catholic youths carrying knives near the bishop.

During a public function for civil servants and the military in Dili on Friday Belo publically apologised for the killing and called on East Timorese to work towards achieving peace in the troubled former Portuguese colony.

East Timor was invaded by Indonesia in December 1975 and declared its 27th province the following year in an act not recognised by the United Nations, which regards Portugal as being the territory's administering power.
